subject: Clarify SOC 2 coverage for Dedicated pools and Private/VPC deployments
messages:
From: Sara Mills <sara.mills@acme.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: security-audit@acme.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 scope question — dedicated pools & on-prem

Hi Jonas,

Quick question as we kick off our 2024 supplier audit: can you confirm whether Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report and any bridge letter cover (a) Hosted API usage, (b) Dedicated / reserved GPU pools we reserve through Redwood Dedicated, and (c) Private/VPC or on-prem deployments where we run a customer-managed instance? Our auditor (BlueGate) flagged different requirements depending on deployment.

Specifically:
- If Acme buys a dedicated pool (reserved capacity) that is dedicated to our account, is that in-scope under your Type II?
- For Private/VPC/on-prem packages, do we need a separate attestation or bridge?

We'd like to know what evidence you can provide and whether a bridge letter is available with dates for the 2024 audit window (Jan 1–Dec 31, 2024).

Thanks — trying to lock scope before we send the questionnaire.

Sara Mills
Head of Vendor Risk
Acme Corp
[Attachment: initial-acme-audit-reqs.pdf (PDF)]

Hi Sara — thanks for the early heads-up. Short answers up-front: hosted API usage is covered by our SOC 2 Type II report; dedicated pools typically *are* eligible for coverage but there are caveats; private/on-prem deployments generally require a separate arrangement (see below).

I looped in Kimberly (Security & Compliance) and Marcus (your account lead) to confirm details and share the right artifacts. Can you confirm BlueGate's auditor contact (I have audits@bluegate.com cc'd) and whether you need a signed bridge letter or a bridge letter template to include in your package?

Next steps I propose:
- Kimberly to confirm the precise language we can use for dedicated (scoped by tenancy model and control ownership).
- If Acme needs a signed bridge for 2024, we can produce one covering the audit window for hosted + "Redwood-managed dedicated pools".
- For Private/VPC/on-prem, we'll outline what we can attest to (control design) and what falls to customer-managed controls.

Cheers,

Jonas Weber

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SOC 2 scope question — dedicated pools & on-prem

Hi Sara (and team),

Thanks for the clear questions — here's how Redwood treats each deployment modality for SOC 2 coverage. I'll keep this high level and attach the SOC 2 report + a bridge-letter template for clarity.

1) Hosted API (Redwood-hosted shared endpoints)
   - In-scope: Yes. Our SOC 2 Type II report covers the hosted control environment, including logical access, change management, and availability controls for our public endpoints.

2) Redwood Dedicated (Reserved GPU pools)
   - Typical case: If the dedicated pool is provisioned as Redwood-managed infrastructure and is assigned exclusively to your account (tenant isolation), we include that infrastructure under the scope of the Type II provided the customer does not manage the host-level controls or networking that materially affect control design.
   - Exceptions: If Acme deploys agents or manages host/network controls for the dedicated pool (customer-managed host/networking), that portion of the environment falls outside our tested scope — we can document the boundary in a bridge letter but the auditor will treat those controls as customer responsibility.

3) Private / VPC / On-prem
   - In general: Private/VPC deployments where the customer controls the host or networking are *not* included in the standard Redwood Type II. We can provide control design documentation and, where applicable, a statement of applicability. For fully-managed VPC offerings where Redwood controls the host/network and we operate the runtime, we can evaluate adding the environment to our scope on a case-by-case basis (contract + audit window permitting).

Bridge letters and evidence
   - We can provide:
     * A standard SOC 2 Type II report (attached).
     * A bridge letter that documents the audit boundary and explicitly states which hosting modes and tenant configurations are included for the audit window you specify. Attached is a draft bridge-letter template (fillable).
     * Supporting artifacts (control narratives, change log snapshots, and recent penetration test summary on request).

Attachments included: SOC2_TypeII_2024_Report.pdf (redacted), bridge_letter-dedicated-vpc-template.docx

Action items for Acme to confirm:
   - Whether your Dedicated pool is Redwood-managed (we provision and operate) or customer-managed (you operate hosts/network).
   - Desired audit window for the bridge (you mentioned Jan 1–Dec 31, 2024).

I'll note one practical detail: bridge letters must reference specific tenant IDs and reservation IDs for dedicated pools so auditors can tie controls to the environment. If you share those IDs, we can draft the letter and route for signature.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2_TypeII_2024_Report.pdf (PDF, 2.3MB)]

Kimberly — thank you, that's very helpful. A couple quick clarifications:

1) Acme's Dedicated pool will be provisioned by Redwood and operated by Redwood (we will not control hosts or networking) — so that sounds like it should be in-scope. We'll provide the reservation/tenant IDs once provisioning completes.

2) For Private/VPC: we expected to retain some host/network controls, so we understand that will likely be out-of-scope for Redwood's Type II; please include explicit language in the bridge template that calls this out so our auditor can mark those as customer responsibilities.

3) Audit window: please draft the bridge letter for Jan 1–Dec 31, 2024. We will need a signed PDF for our audit package.

Can you also confirm turnaround time to get a signed bridge letter once we provide tenant IDs? BlueGate is asking for the signed letter by May 2.
